 GAME THREAD: Miami Heat (6-6) seek fourth straight win in rematch against Detroit Pistons (8-3)
 126 Comments 
 / By 
 Surya Fernandez 
 / November 14, 2026 
 (Photo courtesy of the NBA) 
 The Miami Heat are back in action tonight at Kaseya Center, hosting the Detroit Pistons as they look to extend their winning streak to four games and move above .500 for the first time this season.
 After opening the 2026-27 campaign with four consecutive losses, Miami has turned things around in impressive fashion. The Heat enter Saturday night’s matchup with a 6-6 record following a 133-121 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Friday.
 That victory marked Miami’s third consecutive win and improved its record to 6-2 over its last eight games, providing a much-needed boost after a difficult opening stretch.
 But tonight presents another significant challenge.
 The Pistons enter the matchup at 8-3 and have been one of the Eastern Conference’s stronger teams to open the season. Cade Cunningham is coming off a remarkable 52-point, 11-assist performance in Detroit’s double-overtime victory over the Washington Wizards.
 Detroit also handed Miami one of its early-season losses, defeating the Heat 128-111 at Kaseya Center on October 23. Former Heat sharpshooter Duncan Robinson connected on five three-pointers in that matchup, while John Collins added 23 points.
 The Pistons will be without starting center Jalen Duren tonight, potentially giving Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo an advantage inside.
 Miami, however, faces its own challenges. The Heat are playing on the second night of a back-to-back, and Erik Spoelstra will once again need contributions throughout the rotation as the team navigates injuries and lineup changes.
 Can the Heat avenge their earlier loss to Detroit, make it four consecutive victories and climb above .500?
 STARTING LINEUPS
 Miami Heat 
 Davion Mitchell, PG
 Tim Hardaway Jr., SG
 Myron Gardner, SF
 Giannis Antetokounmpo, PF
 Bam Adebayo, C

 INJURY REPORT / PLAYER AVAILABILITY
 Miami Heat 
 Klay Thompson — OUT (left ankle sprain)
 Pelle Larsson — OUT (illness)
 Vladislav Goldin — OUT (G League/two-way assignment)
 Giannis Antetokounmpo — Expected to play (right wrist sprain)
 Detroit Pistons 
 Jalen Duren — OUT (right hamstring strain)
 Isaiah Joe — OUT (right hip contusion)
 Chaz Lanier — OUT (G League assignment)
 Ebuka Okorie — OUT (G League assignment)
 Ugonna Onyenso — OUT (G League/two-way assignment)
 GAME INFO
 Matchup:  Detroit Pistons (8-3) at Miami Heat (6-6)
 Date:  Saturday, November 14, 2026
 Time:  8:00 PM ET
 Location:  Kaseya Center — Miami, Florida
 TV:  NBA TV / WPLG Local 10 (South Florida)
 Radio:  560 AM WQAM / HEAT Radio Network
 The Heat have finally found some momentum, but tonight offers another opportunity to prove their turnaround is for real against one of the East’s stronger early-season teams.
 Will Miami make it four straight and finally move above .500?
 Join the conversation below, share your reactions throughout the game and cheer on the Heat with the Hot Hot Hoops community!
